official_geography_or_purpose: Official Cook Islands shipping policy groups Pukapuka, Nassau, Palmerston, Rakahanga, Manihiki and Penrhyn for Northern Group service. This packet has only its four named current members; two official service islands are outside this slice. It is not a complete northern islands polygon.
review_result_and_limit: Partial Northern Group service geography; missing service islands are outside this packet, not an atlas omission finding.

official_geography_or_purpose: National jurisdiction consists of dispersed islands and the Southern outer-island shipping group includes Aitutaki, Atiu, Mitiaro, Mauke and Mangaia. This area slice owns seven atlas locations but is not a full island-government census: Rarotonga is the main island and other named territories are owned in the separate Northern slice.
review_result_and_limit: Treat each physical island/atoll and outer-island service group separately. Review source role, lagoon masks and named minor islands.

The exact geoBoundaries commune feature contains both, while current atlas polygon omits source component near Sala y Gómez.
review_result_and_limit: Correction-needed; preserve commune identity and parent; follow up one bounded issue for the off-island component and verify current member points before a separate edit.

official_geography_or_purpose: Two separately named U.S. Fish and Wildlife refuges; each refuge includes far more submerged marine area than terrestrial island. The area is a geographic group, not a legal single refuge or land polygon.
review_result_and_limit: Preserve the two island locations separately; never substitute refuge/monument marine limits for dry-land outlines.

official_geography_or_purpose: Kiribati official sources distinguish the Line Islands and enumerate eight Kiribati islands; the physical chain also includes U.S. territories Jarvis and Palmyra (and Kingman Reef). Current area is larger than this packet slice; only three area members are assigned here.
review_result_and_limit: Cross-sovereignty group; keep Kiribati and U.S. parentage separate. Existing KIR ADM1 source has only 3 group features and a blank canonical level, so do not treat its Line feature as complete without island-by-island test.

official_geography_or_purpose: Official French Polynesia maritime source calls the Marquesas an archipelago of about 20 islands/islets/seamounts, six inhabited in northern and southern island subgroups.
review_result_and_limit: Archipelago is semantically supported; six inhabited or 20 physical component counts are not polygon completeness tests. Check uninhabited islands and source-scale omission.

official_geography_or_purpose: UNESCO identifies Henderson as the largest of the four Pitcairn-group islands; Pitcairn is the only inhabited island. Only Henderson is scoped in this packet.
review_result_and_limit: Preserve four-island parent meaning and one scoped Henderson unit; source admin1 polygon is the group, not a dedicated validated Henderson shoreline.

official_geography_or_purpose: French Polynesia maritime source divides the Society archipelago into Windward and Leeward groups; both are present and two members are scoped here.
review_result_and_limit: Nested regional subgroup names are official service/planning geography; do not overstate as two commune/province statutory jurisdictions or infer every islet from Natural Earth counts.

official_geography_or_purpose: Official French Polynesia service describes the combined Tuamotu-Gambier archipelago and a deconcentrated government circumscription; planning services also expose Tuamotu-Gambier plans.
review_result_and_limit: One valid combined service/archipelago grouping; do not split or claim ADM-level law from the 1:10m generalized outline.

official_geography_or_purpose: Official French Polynesia maritime source identifies five principal high islands: Tubuai, Rurutu, Rimatara, Raivavae and Rapa. This packet scopes the aggregate group, not each island separately.
review_result_and_limit: Named group has a supported role; the aggregation must be checked for source-era, small-islet omission and coastline representation.
